description: The National Response Framework is the US guide to how the nation responds to all types of disasters and emergencies, built on the concepts of the National Incident Management System and aimed at jurisdictions, citizens, non-governmental organisations and businesses. The fourth edition (2019) introduced community lifelines, used to spot breakdowns in essential services and judge immediate and potential disaster impacts. Federal response is organised into 15 Emergency Support Functions: transportation; communications; public works and engineering; firefighting; information and planning; mass care; logistics; public health and medical services; search and rescue; oil and hazardous materials; agriculture and natural resources; energy; public safety and security; cross-sector business and infrastructure (ESF 14); and external affairs, with six support annexes. It is published by FEMA as free downloadable PDFs of the framework, a training guide and each ESF annex, and succeeds the earlier National Response Plan. Caveats: it is doctrine, not data, and roles and lifeline definitions change between editions. It supports the design of emergency response and restoration scenarios that follow real US coordination structures, including cross-sector infrastructure dependencies; a related record is the US National Infrastructure Protection Plan.
